papers.title: An ancient Hippo-dystrophin axis controls cortical stability and multicellular interactions in a close unicellular relative of animals
papers.abstract: How the protein complexes and signal transduction pathways that regulate animal physiology and human disease emerged over evolutionary time remains poorly understood. The dystrophin-dystroglycan complex (DGC), whose disruption causes muscular dystrophy in humans, is best known for its role in maintaining muscle integrity and was previously thought to have originated in animals. Here we show that Capsaspora owczarzaki, a close unicellular relative of animals, encodes core DGC components- including a bona fide dystroglycan ortholog- as critical downstream targets of the Hippo pathway. Loss of Capsaspora dystrophin (coDystrophin) destabilizes the cortical actin cytoskeleton, causes excessive membrane blebbing, and produces flattened, irregularly shaped multicellular aggregates, all of which phenocopy loss of coYki. Conversely, coDystrophin overexpression rescues the cytoskeletal defects of coYki mutant cells, identifying coDystrophin as a key effector of Hippo signaling. Despite extensive rearrangement of dystrophin domain architecture during animal evolution, a human microdystrophin partially rescues coDystrophin mutant cells, revealing deep functional conservation. These findings show that core DGC components predate animals and indicate that the complex's ancestral role was not muscle-specific but lay in maintaining cortical cytoskeletal integrity under the control of an ancient Hippo-regulated genetic module.

papers.title: A comprehensive Drosophila toolkit reveals context-dependent functional hierarchies across RasG12X variants in vivo
papers.abstract: KRAS is a GTPase regulating key signalling processes involved in cell proliferation, differentiation, growth and survival. KRAS is the most prevalent oncogene in human cancers, often acquiring a point mutation at Glycine 12 (G12). Although several possible amino acid substitutions occur at this hotspot in humans, most animal cancer models often examine only a single or limited subset of G12X variants, restricting our understanding of their distinct biological effects. Here, we describe a novel transgenic toolkit in Drosophila melanogaster comparing the most frequently observed oncogenic G12X variants (G12A, G12C, G12D, G12R, G12S, G12V), and evaluate these across multiple developmental and tumour contexts in vivo. Interestingly, we demonstrate how the phenotypic strength of each G12X variant differs significantly depending on the biological context, highlighting the importance of considering these point mutations systematically. Overall, our comprehensive RasG12X toolkit provides a powerful and versatile platform to explore the dysregulation of KRAS in vivo, serving as a valuable resource enabling unprecedented opportunities to investigate variant- and context-specific mechanisms of oncogenic signalling with direct relevance to cancer biology and therapy.

papers.title: Genetically Encoded Photodecaging of Asparagine Enables Protein Function Control and Time-Resolved N-Glycosylation
papers.abstract: Asparagine contributes to protein function through its polar carboxamide side chain and serves as the acceptor residue for N-linked glycosylation, yet temporally controlling these roles directly through the side-chain carboxamide remains challenging. Here, we report the genetic encoding of N4-(2-nitrobenzyl)-L-asparagine (ONBN), a photocaged asparagine that regenerates the native side-chain carboxamide upon 365 nm irradiation. Engineered aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs enabled site-specific ONBN incorporation into proteins in Escherichia coli and mammalian cells. Photodecaging restored Renilla luciferase activity and activated TRAF6 polyubiquitination mediated by UBE2N in living cells. Beyond active-site residues, we further developed CAGE-proxN, using computationally guided proximal caging to optically activate firefly luciferase. Finally, ONBN incorporation at the acceptor position of an N-glycosylation sequon enabled light-triggered initiation and time-resolved monitoring of post-translational glycan installation on an endoplasmic reticulum-targeted reporter. Variation of the -2 flanking residue revealed sequence-dependent differences in apparent glycosylation kinetics. This work extends genetically encoded photocontrol to the asparagine carboxamide and provides a platform for investigating asparagine-dependent protein functions and the temporal regulation of N-glycosylation in living cells.

papers.title: FGF activates Wnt signaling during newt lens regeneration
papers.abstract: Newts regenerate their eye lens following its complete removal. To accomplish this, pigmented epithelial cells located in the dorsal iris transdifferentiate to lens epithelial cells. FGF and Wnt signaling pathways have been implicated during this process, but their association remained unclear. Here, we used FGF signaling inhibitors to stall lens regeneration and studied the affected downstream mechanisms using immunofluorescence, western blotting, and RNAseq. We showed that entry to the cell cycle was slowed, ERK levels were lower, and several genes were differentially regulated with FGF inhibition. Among the impacted genes were Wnt signaling modulators revealing a potential connection between the pathways. FGF inhibition also stalled the gradual increase in beta-catenin abundance in the nucleus and junctions in iris pigmented epithelial cells during lens regeneration. To place Wnt downstream of the FGF signaling pathway, we pharmacologically activated Wnt and showed that it is sufficient to rescue the lens regeneration stalling phenotype observed with FGF inhibition. Overall, our data indicate that FGF activates the Wnt signaling pathway during newt lens regeneration.

papers.title: Roe deer embryonic diapause is associated with reduced oxidative phosphorylation and altered lipid metabolism
papers.abstract: Conceptus elongation is a shared feature of preimplantation development in roe deer and cattle. However, unlike cattle embryos, roe deer embryos undergo embryonic diapause prior to elongation, during which blastocyst growth remains markedly reduced for 4-5 months before development rapidly resumes. To investigate the molecular basis of these developmental differences, we assembled a novel roe deer reference genome and analyzed single-embryo transcriptomes from diapausing and elongated roe deer conceptuses, comparing their transcriptomes with those of cattle embryos from day 6 morulae to day 14 tubular conceptuses. Pseudotime and principal component analyses revealed parallel developmental trajectories across species and distinct gene-expression profiles during diapause. Roe deer diapause embryos exhibited reduced transcriptional signatures of oxidative phosphorylation, mitochondrial biogenesis and protein glycosylation pathways relative to cattle blastocysts, while maintaining expression of lineage-specification markers, consistent with continued differentiation despite a metabolically quiescent state. While roe deer retained the function of the corpus luteum during diapause and continued to secrete progesterone, they did not express interferon-{tau} upon elongation. Elongation of roe deer embryos triggered robust upregulation of cell-cycle regulators, ribosomal biogenesis and oxidative-phosphorylation genes, aligning with the high energetic demands of elongation. By contrasting a diapause and non-diapause species, we illuminated the genomic and metabolic frameworks that underlie this unique reproductive adaptation of diapause and elongation.

papers.title: Continuous ex utero development of mouse zygotes to early organogenesis
papers.abstract: In mammals, embryogenesis normally unfolds within the uterus, limiting direct access to the developmental processes that transform a zygote into an embryo with forming organs. Although mouse embryos can be cultured ex utero from early post-implantation stages to mid-gestation, continuous culture from the zygote into organogenesis has not been achieved. Through comparative single-cell transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses, here we discover aberrant BMP signaling and suboptimal metabolic support as barriers to continuous ex utero development. BMP inhibition, together with stage-specific optimization of the culture environment, enables mouse zygotes to progress through peri-implantation development, gastrulation, and into early organogenesis ex utero. Cultured embryos form major embryonic and extraembryonic lineages, establish body axes, and generate multiple organ primordia, while retaining developmental delays and molecular differences from in vivo embryos. By connecting developmental stages that have previously been cultured separately, this study provides an accessible platform for dissecting how early mammalian development progresses into organ formation and a reference for evaluating stem-cell-based embryo models.

papers.title: CSF Boundary Disruption and Tumor-Dependent Patterns of Medulloblastoma Metastasis
papers.abstract: Background: Leptomeningeal metastasis is the major cause of mortality in medulloblastoma, yet the mechanisms that facilitate dissemination are poorly resolved. Here, we leveraged preclinical models to define metastatic topology, the anatomical distribution and organization of disseminated disease across craniospinal compartments and ask how topology is influenced by cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) access, primary tumor anatomy, and tumor biology. Methods: Orthotopic D425 xenograft models were used to manipulate primary tumor geometry, defined by anatomical position of primary tumors within the cerebellum relative to CSF facing boundaries. Longitudinal bioluminescence, survival, primary growth architecture at the tumor host interface, CSF boundary breach, and craniospinal metastatic distribution were quantified. Additional medulloblastoma models MED411, MED2112, and CHLA-01-MED were implanted at a common midline cerebellar location to assess tumor-intrinsic contributions to metastatic topology. Results: While primary tumor geometry altered disease progression and survival, it did not significantly alter metastasis distribution. Strikingly, growth architecture and primary tumor burden correlated with dissemination. Despite their large size, circumscribed tumors frequently remained localized, whereas smaller, disruptive primary growth architecture was strongly associated with boundary breach, intracranial, and spinal dissemination. Conversely, when anatomical origin was held constant, distinct medulloblastoma models generated significantly different metastatic topologies. Conclusions: Disruption of CSF-facing anatomical boundaries is associated with distant dissemination, whereas the distribution of established metastatic disease differs substantially among medulloblastoma models despite standardized implantation conditions. These findings distinguish anatomical factors associated with dissemination from tumor-dependent patterns of metastatic colonization and establish an experimental framework for investigating the mechanisms underlying metastatic topology.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Vascular Wall Cells during Ductus Arteriosus Development and Closure
papers.abstract: Background: The transition from fetal to postnatal circulation requires closure of the ductus arteriosus (DA), involving smooth muscle cell contraction followed by anatomical remodeling. However, the spatial organization and developmental transcriptional dynamics of vascular wall cells during this transition remain poorly understood. Methods: We analyzed vascular morphology and spatial transcript profiles of the mouse DA and aorta at five stages from embryonic day 14.5 (E14.5) to postnatal day 2.5 (P2.5), enabling paired comparisons within tissue sections. Selected findings were compared with an independent mouse single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset. Histological and spatial transcript analyses were also performed on human DA tissue and the adjacent pulmonary artery. Results: The DA exhibited transiently higher cell-cycle-associated transcription across multiple vascular wall populations at E16.5, preceding medial thickening at E18.5 and postnatal luminal closure. Prenatally, DA mural cells exhibited greater contractile-associated gene expression than aortic mural cells. This difference diminished after birth, accompanied by a marked shift toward synthetic-like transcriptional programs associated with extracellular matrix remodeling and proteolysis. Ductal endothelial cells exhibited postnatal divergence from aortic endothelial cells in matrix- and adhesion-associated gene expression. Adventitial fibroblasts displayed distinct extracellular matrix- and insulin-like growth factor-associated expression profiles. In a human postnatal DA specimen, synthetic-like mural cells were enriched in regions of disrupted elastic lamellae and prominent collagen staining and shared selected remodeling-associated markers with postnatal mouse DA mural cells. Conclusions: DA development and closure involve temporally organized transcriptional changes across vascular wall populations, characterized by prenatal cell-cycle-associated activity and rapid postnatal reorganization of mural transcriptional programs. These findings provide a spatial framework for understanding vascular cell plasticity and multicellular remodeling during DA closure.

papers.title: DDB2 localizes to the nucleolus to mediate oxaliplatin resistance in colorectal cancer
papers.abstract: Despite the widespread use of platinum drugs in cancer therapy, defining their mechanisms of action and predicting clinical outcomes remain challenging. Unlike cisplatin, which kills cells mainly through the DNA damage response, oxaliplatin toxicity is driven largely by nucleolar stress, yet how cells cope with this stress remains poorly understood. A nucleotide excision repair protein, damage-specific DNA binding protein 2 (DDB2), protects cells from oxaliplatin but not cisplatin, suggesting that it may preferentially engage oxaliplatin adducts. Using single-molecule analysis of DNA-binding proteins from nuclear extracts, we show that DDB2 binds both oxaliplatin and cisplatin intrastrand adducts. Oxaliplatin, but not cisplatin, drives progressive accumulation of DDB2 in nucleoli, pointing to a role at sites of oxaliplatin-induced nucleolar stress. The repair-deficient xeroderma pigmentosum group E K244E variant localizes to nucleoli but fails to rescue oxaliplatin sensitivity of DDB2-knockout cells, indicating that repair activity, not nucleolar localization alone, is required for protection. In colorectal cancer (CRC), elevated DDB2 levels correlate with higher oxaliplatin IC50, are higher in tumors than adjacent normal tissue by immunohistochemistry, and DDB2 transcript associates with non-response and shorter progression-free survival in FOLFOX-treated patients. Pharmacological inactivation or degradation of DDB2 synergizes with oxaliplatin, offering a biomarker-driven strategy to overcome chemoresistance.

papers.title: A conserved ubiquitin signalling module controls membrane raft integrity at the neuronal synapse
papers.abstract: Activity-dependent ubiquitination of synaptic proteins is one of the key contributors of synaptic plasticity, along with localized protein synthesis and ubiquitin-dependent protein turnover. Substantial changes in the protein composition occur in the postsynaptic density upon chronic activation or inhibition of primary neurons. Precisely how a large-scale regulation of ensembles of synaptic proteins occurs through the ubiquitin proteasome system remains unknown. MAGE-D1 is a highly conserved protein enriched in brain and its deletion in mice leads to a range of behavioral phenotypes including defects in learning, memory and a complete resistance to cocaine addiction. Here, we found that MAGE-D1 acts as a scaffold bridging the ubiquitin ligase Praja-1 and the deubiquitinase Usp7. This MAGE-D1 signalling module directly interacts with and regulates the levels of Brain acid-soluble protein-1 (BASP1) which is a key component and stabilizer of neuronal membrane rafts. Disruption of MAGE-D1 complex function or chemical inhibition of Usp7 in mice results in resistance to cocaine-induced locomotor sensitization accompanied by specific degradation of oligomeric BASP1 and other key synaptic proteins in the postsynaptic density of mice thalamus. As a result, loss of MAGE-D1 in differentiated neurons leads to a dramatic disorganization of neuronal membrane rafts and anomalies in the synaptic membrane protein landscape. Finally, we mapped the structural architecture of the human MAGE-D1/Praja-1/Usp7 complex revealing the basis for the scaffolding nature of MAGE-D1. In summary, we discovered a conserved synaptic ubiquitin signalling network mediated by a protein complex that localizes to the synapse and regulates structures of membrane rafts and actin cytoskeleton.

papers.title: Nerve and vascular abnormalities precede loss of corneal transparency in Pax6-haploinsufficient mice
papers.abstract: Aniridia-associated keratopathy (AAK), caused by PAX6 haploinsufficiency, progresses from a clinically clear cornea to opacity, neovascularization, and abnormal innervation, but when disease-associated changes first emerge remains unclear. We combined corneal nerve imaging, CD31 immunolabeling, transmission electron microscopy, and RNA sequencing of whole cornea from Pax6Sey-Neu/+mice at postnatal day 3-4, day 15, and adulthood. Corneal transcripts were analyzed using curated axon-guidance, myelination, and vascular/lymphatic gene panels. Mutant corneas showed reduced nerve density and persistent stromal fascicles beginning during the first postnatal week. Peripheral vascular structures were present in both genotypes at birth; these resolved during normal maturation but persisted and extended centrally in mutant corneas by two weeks, before loss of transparency. Transcriptomic analysis identified widespread differences between genotypes while both corneas remained transparent, with the strongest and most coherent changes involving vascular and lymphatic genes. Wild-type corneas silenced an endothelial and lymphatic expression program between postnatal day 15 and adulthood, whereas mutant corneas retained expression of this program. Individual axon-guidance genes differed between genotypes, but axon-guidance did not show program-level expansion in transparent corneas. Compact stromal myelin was restricted to opaque regions. These findings identify early vascular and neural abnormalities that precede corneal opacity and establish that a transparent Pax6-haploinsufficient cornea is already pathologically altered.

papers.title: Constraint-Based Pan-Cancer Metabolic Modeling Identifies Medium-Robust Biomarkers and Broad-Spectrum Anticancer Targets
papers.abstract: Background: Cancer metabolic reprogramming varies across tumour types and nutrient environments, complicating the identification of robust metabolic biomarkers and therapeutic targets. We developed a constraint based pancancer framework to identify medium robust metabolic alterations and broadly effective candidate enzyme targets. Methods: Transcriptomic profiles from 33 TCGA cancer types were integrated with Recon3D to reconstruct cancer and healthy tissue specific genome scale metabolic models. Parsimonious multiobjective metabolite flow variability analysis was performed under five nutrient conditions to classify differential rates of metabolite synthesis, uptake, and secretion. An extended Anticancer Target Discovery framework incorporating fuzzy multiobjective optimization was employed to evaluate candidate enzyme perturbations based on cancer cell inhibition, ATP suppression, preservation of healthy tissue metabolism, and robustness across nutrient conditions. Findings: The models predicted recurrent increases in cardiolipin-related lipid synthesis and aromatic amino acid metabolism, enhanced uptake of essential amino acids and choline, and elevated lactate secretion across multiple cancer medium combinations. CRLS1 emerged as the most broadly effective predicted enzyme target, satisfying the treatment criteria across all 165 cancer medium combinations, whereas PGS1 and PTPMT1 exhibited broad but incomplete coverage. These findings highlight mitochondrial phospholipid metabolism as a potential shared vulnerability across cancer types and provide testable candidates for metabolomic and experimental validation.

papers.title: Autumn warming decouples the molecular control of photosynthesis and cold acclimation from growth cessation in white spruce
papers.abstract: {middle dot} In evergreen conifers, late-season photosynthetic downregulation is typically coordinated with growth cessation and the induction of cold acclimation, a key component of winter adaptation. However, the transcriptional basis of this coordination and its sensitivity to warming and drought remain poorly understood. {middle dot} To investigate the molecular basis of these responses, we examined how summer drought, autumn warming and their combination affect the expression of photosynthetic and cold-acclimation genes in white spruce, and whether responses differ among families from different latitudes. {middle dot} Autumn warming sustained photosynthetic gene expression into early winter while suppressing cold-acclimation genes, demonstrating that photosynthetic and cold-acclimation networks become decoupled from growth cessation, which remained largely unchanged. Although cold acclimation models derived from herbaceous species predict regulation through CBF pathways, canonical CBF/DREB regulators showed little transcriptional response. Instead, warming-induced suppression of cold acclimation was mediated by MYB- and AP2/ERF-centered regulatory networks, indicating a distinct conifer mechanism. Northern and southern families also differed in their transcriptional responses to warming despite exhibiting similar growth-cessation phenology. {middle dot} Together, these findings identify regulatory networks through which warmer autumns disrupt seasonal coordination in boreal conifers, potentially increasing susceptibility to freezing injury, limiting spring recovery, and ultimately affecting forest carbon sequestration.

papers.title: Targeting ATR-CHK1-WEE1 signaling enhances IMPDH inhibitor efficacy in mTORC1-driven tumor cells
papers.abstract: Uncontrolled activation of the master metabolic regulator Mechanistic Target of Rapamycin Complex 1 (mTORC1) in tumors confers strong dependence on the guanylate nucleotide synthesis enzyme inosine-5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH) for tumor cell growth and viability. Clinically approved IMPDH inhibitors reduce the guanylate nucleotide pool available for DNA synthesis in mTORC1-driven tumor cells, resulting in prolonged DNA replication stress and accumulation of DNA damage that culminates in apoptosis. These early molecular events are accompanied by activation of adaptive DNA replication stress response (RSR) and DNA damage response (DDR) pathways. We hypothesized that targeting these adaptive responses could enhance IMPDH inhibitor efficacy. We find that combining IMPDH inhibition with inhibition of the ATR-CHK1-WEE1 signaling axis increases the efficacy and durability of response in cell models, and in a syngeneic xenograft tumor model of the mTORC1-driven genetic tumor syndrome Tuberous Sclerosis Complex. Mechanistically, abrogating ATR-CHK1-WEE1 signaling during prolonged IMPDH inhibition causes aberrant cell cycle progression, increased DNA double-strand breaks, and formation of micronuclei. Together these findings uncover adaptive mechanisms that restrict IMPDH inhibitor efficacy, informing a combination strategy to improve treatment efficacy, while maintaining selectivity for targeting tumor cells that are driven by uncontrolled mTORC1 activation.

papers.title: Fishing for new immunotherapy compounds to boost innate tumor rejection
papers.abstract: Despite significant advances in cancer immunotherapy, tackling immunosuppression remains critical to achieve more effective responses. While developing the zebrafish xenograft model, we found that some human tumors engraft very efficiently ("progressors"), while others are cleared by the host ("regressors"). We showed that this was dependent on innate immunity, which recognizes and eliminates some cancer cells, while others are able to evade and suppress it. This opened an opportunity to perform an in vivo phenotypic drug screen to find compounds that induce clearance by boosting innate-tumor rejection. Zebrafish xenografts of human colorectal (CRC) and breast cancer (BC) that show a high engraftment/low clearance phenotype were used to screen over 500 FDA-approved small-molecule compounds, with tumor clearance serving as the phenotypic readout. The screen identified 23 hit compounds, of which six were effective across both cancer models. Mechanism-of-action enrichment analysis revealed a significant overrepresentation of autonomic nervous system-targeting drugs among the hits, particularly cholinergic ones. Immune profiling in myeloid reporter lines showed that the lead hit, Tiotropium bromide, a muscarinic receptor antagonist, reprograms tumor-associated macrophages toward a pro-inflammatory, anti-tumoral state. Tiotropium significantly increased macrophage phagocytosis, and macrophage depletion completely abolished its pro-clearance activity, establishing these myeloid cells as essential effectors. In a syngeneic CT26 colorectal mouse model, Tiotropium synergized with anti-PD-1 to control tumor growth and improve survival, outperforming all monotherapy arms. This effect was immune-dependent, as it was lost in immunodeficient NSG mice. Together, these findings demonstrate that in vivo phenotypic screening of FDA-approved compounds in zebrafish xenografts is a productive strategy for innate immune drug discovery in cancer. The identification of Tiotropium as a myeloid-reprogramming innate immune primer, together with the unbiased recovery of the neuro-immune axis as a druggable target, opens new avenues for overcoming immunotherapy resistance.

papers.title: Lactation is an Exercise-Responsive Window for Intergenerational Metabolic Programming
papers.abstract: Maternal exercise during pregnancy can influence offspring metabolic health, but whether exercise initiated exclusively during lactation has lasting effects is less clear. We investigated the effects of postpartum exercise in chow-fed and high-fat diet (HFD)-fed dams and followed their offspring after weaning. Female C57BL/6J mice consumed chow or a 60% HFD before mating and throughout lactation. Beginning on postpartum day 1, dams were assigned to sedentary or treadmill-exercise conditions until weaning on day 25. Offspring were maintained on chow and assessed longitudinally for body mass, body composition, glucose tolerance, and insulin tolerance through adulthood. Postpartum exercise reduced maternal adiposity and improved maternal glucose tolerance, with effects observed in both chow- and HFD-fed dams. Maternal postpartum exercise was associated with altered offspring growth trajectories and body composition, with effects becoming more apparent with advancing age. Glucose tolerance also improved with maternal exercise in adult male and female offspring, whereas insulin tolerance did not differ significantly among maternal treatment groups. These findings suggest that maternal exercise during lactation is associated with long-term differences in offspring metabolic health that persist long after cessation of the maternal intervention and become increasingly apparent in adulthood. Our findings expand the exercise-responsive window for developmental metabolic programming beyond pregnancy and support lactation as a potentially modifiable period during which maternal physical activity may influence long-term offspring metabolic health.

papers.title: Morphological and transcriptomic renal characteristics of dioxin-induced fetal obstructive uropathy
papers.abstract: Congenital obstructive uropathy (COU) is an important cause of childhood kidney failure, yet understanding its variable renal outcomes and genetic modifiers is limited by the lack of genotype-independent models of in utero obstruction. Here, we characterized renal morphology and gene expression at embryonic day (E)18.5 in a mouse model of COU induced by exposure to 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (dioxin) at E10.5. Dioxin exposure reproducibly induced bilateral hydroureteronephrosis with selective medullary flattening with relatively preserved renal architecture. Transcriptomic analysis revealed altered developmental, cell cycle, metabolic, innate immune, and toxin response programs, alongside changes in cell-type-associated signatures. However, immunohistochemistry showed no differences in the abundance of examined stromal and proximal tubular populations, suggesting altered cellular states rather than changes in cellular composition. Together with morphology consistent with early obstructive responses and the absence of prominent injury markers, these findings support its use as a non-genetic model to investigate how congenital obstruction perturbs renal development.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics atlas of Echinococcus granulosusreveals germinative cell heterogeneity and candidate developmental key genes
papers.abstract: Cystic echinococcosis is a zoonotic parasitic disease caused by infection with Echinococcus granulosus. Progressive cyst growth can compress host tissues and elicit immune responses. Characterizing the cellular composition and lineage differentiation of E. granulosus protoscoleces may provide insight into the regulation of parasite proliferation and development and facilitate the identification of potential intervention targets. We generated a single-cell transcriptomic atlas of E. granulosus and identified six major cell populations: Germinative cell, Muscle, Neuron, Storage, Tegument,and Cilium. Germinative cells were heterogeneous: some retained an undifferentiated transcriptional profile, whereas others expressed genes associated with differentiated cell types, consistent with the initiation of lineage-associated programs. RNA velocity analysis suggested four potential trajectories, one involving transitions within the undifferentiated population that may contribute to self-renewal and homeostasis, and three showing trends toward distinct lineage-associated subpopulations. A p53 homolog and threonine dehydrogenase tdh were identified as candidate developmental key genes that may contribute to larval growth and development. This study provides a single-cell atlas of E. granulosus protoscoleces and identifies key candidate genes involved in larval development, providing a foundation for future functional studies and the exploration of potential anthelmintic targets.

papers.title: Allele-specific open chromatin analysis revealed allelic bias of alcohol-induced gene expression in human microglia
papers.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a polygenic disorder. Most AUD-associated variants identified by genome-wide association studies (GWAS) are located in non-coding regions, making it challenging to determine which variants are functional and how they contribute to disease-relevant cellular phenotypes. Here, we integrated microglia-specific allele-specific open chromatin (ASoC) mapping, GWAS, eQTLs, differentially expressed genes identified from postmortem human microglia and iPSC-derived microglial-like cells, and chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) data from postmortem microglia to prioritize regulatory variants, followed by functional validation using multiple assays. We identified a panel of AUD-associated non-coding variants, particularly rs7307261, as a candidate functional variant that showed regulatory potential. The minor allele (A) of rs7307261 showed higher predicted similarity to binding motifs for E26 transformation-specific (ETS)-family transcription factors, including FLI1 and ELF2, than the G allele. The A allele was also associated with increased CD163 expression in AUD postmortem microglia and in iPSC-derived microglial-like cells after ethanol exposure. Notably, the ethanol-induced CD163 expression was abolished by knocking out rs7307261 or converting rs7307261 A/A to G/G, accompanied by changes in ethanol-induced microglial phagocytic function. Together, our study provides a framework for translating AUD genetic associations into context-specific functional mechanisms by linking non-coding risk variants to target genes and ethanol-induced cellular phenotypes.

papers.title: Comparative transcriptomic validation of candidate geroprotectors in human iPSC-derived neurons
papers.abstract: The discovery of geroprotectors, defined as interventions that slow aging-related deterioration and preserve function, remains constrained by reliance on lifespan studies. Lifespan studies take years, are costly and resource intensive, and return a whole-organism endpoint dominated in mice by neoplastic death. These studies cannot be readily scaled and do not specify which tissue(s) are protected by geroprotectors. Human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cells provide a scalable alternative that enables defined lineages and genetically diverse donors to be studied in parallel. However, reprogramming resets epigenetic age, and whether iPSC-derived cells can report responses relevant to aging has remained unclear. Here, we evaluated eight candidate geroprotectors in iPSC-derived neurons using multiple classes of aging-associated transcriptomic readouts. Aging-associated pathways, including mTORC1 and MEK-ERK signaling, were intact and pharmacologically tunable in these cells. Genetic background accounted for most transcriptional variance, with compound responses differing in magnitude and reproducibility between donors. PI-103 suppressed the mTORC1 signature and increased DCX and BDNF expression, while also inducing genes associated with older age in two independent human excitatory-neuron references. These findings indicate that distinct aging measures capture different dimensions of drug response and that no single readout is sufficient to define geroprotection in our model. Together, these results support iPSC-derived cells as a scalable screening tool for candidate geroprotectors, enabled by the transcriptional aging readouts now available, with the potential to resolve tissue- and donor-dependent responses as additional lineages and donors are incorporated.

papers.title: Genome-Wide Association Study Identifies Novel Genetic Variants Linked to Meropenem Resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae
papers.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae have emerged as an urgent public health threat in recent years. Infections caused by carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in particular are associated with high rates of mortality, especially in immunocompromised patients. Substantial carbapenem resistance remains unexplained in K. pneumoniae even after accounting for known resistance genes. To uncover unknown mechanisms associated with meropenem resistance, we performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) in 1,705 K. pneumoniae clinical isolates with previously determined resistance profiles to meropenem . We conducted the GWAS by using an elastic net regression to control for genome-wide linkage disequilibrium and combined it with a conditional linear mixed model to control for the presence of genes known to confer carbapenem resistance. The resulting set of variants predicted to be associated with meropenem resistance mapped to genes broadly related to the plasticity of the genome. We developed a visualization tool integrating GWAS results with phenotypic data and polymorphic site information to aid in hypothesis generation, which allowed us to prioritize novel genomic candidates. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of the combined approach in detecting novel genomic variants associated with meropenem resistance in K. pneumoniae, while controlling for strong bacterial population structure, to advance our understanding of the genetic basis of carbapenem resistance.

papers.title: Designing a Saccharomyces cerevisiae Cell Factory for the Overaccumulation of Tyrosol using Rational Design and Genome-Scale Metabolic Modeling Approaches
papers.abstract: Tyrosol (TyOH) is a phenolic compound with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, naturally present in two Mediterranean products, wine and virgin olive oil, and is the key precursor of Hydroxytyrosol or Salidroside. Its industrial production still relies on chemical synthesis, which conflicts with the EU Green Deal roadmap to transition to a clean, circular, resource-efficient economy by 2050. Thus, moving to a sustainable economy is a priority. Here, we engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae as a cell factory to produce TyOH. To support this goal, we used ecFactory, a pipeline leveraging enzyme-constrained genome-scale metabolic models (ecGEMs), to predict gene targets, narrowing the candidate list and simplifying experimental validation for strain development. The modifications were tested in a medium composed mainly of glucose with ammonium sulfate as the sole nitrogen source. The final strain reached 876.91 {+/-} 20.37 mg/L in a 0.5 L bioreactor, demonstrating the potential of model-guided engineering for sustainable TyOH production.

papers.title: Mechanical Induced Stress Enhances Arabidopsis Susceptibility to Fusarium oxysporum in a Jasmonic Acid-Dependent Manner
papers.abstract: Prolonged mechanical-induced stress (MIS) primes juvenile Arabidopsis plants for enhanced resistance against necrotrophic pathogens through the activation of jasmonate-mediated defense pathways. We hypothesised that MIS would weaken defense against hemibiotrophic pathogens that exploit jasmonate pathways to promote infection. We show that touch-acclimated wild-type plants were more susceptible to Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. conglutinans (Foc) infection than un-touched control plants. Jasmonic acid (JA) levels as well as JA defense-related gene expression were hyper-induced for up to 5 days post-inoculation in the MIS plants. In contrast, the MIS- and control- JA biosynthesis-deficient mutant jasmonate resistance 1 (jar1-11) was more resistant to Foc infection compared to the WT. The jar1-11 mutant showed significant attenuation in the induction of JA defense-responsive gene expression. In the absence of Foc infection, a single event of MIS similarly induced JA biosynthesis and stress-associated marker genes, but not JA signalling genes, in naive and touch-acclimated plant tissues. Touch-acclimated plants had higher basal levels of JA and JA defense-related genes expression, including PDF1.2, VSP1, and LOX1. Our findings highlight that prolonged MIS of Arabidopsis cross-primes JA-dependent susceptibility to a hemibiotrophic pathogen that can hijack the JA pathway to promote infection, revealing a potential trade-off when utilising MIS to promote immunity against necrotrophic pathogens or alter morphological traits for agronomical gains.

papers.title: The selective autophagy receptor AtNBR1 associates with lipid droplets during seed germination and contributes to seed longevity
papers.abstract: Lipid droplets, once viewed primarily as lipid storage organelles, are increasingly recognized as key regulators of cellular homeostasis, which is particularly critical during seed imbibition and germination. Here, we investigated the role of the selective autophagy receptor AtNBR1 in lipid droplet-associated processes during Arabidopsis seed germination. AtNBR1 and ATG8 proteins were specifically and transiently recruited to lipid droplets during germination. Confocal imaging revealed their predominant colocalization in condensate-like puncta adjacent to lipid droplets and, less frequently, in autophagosome-like structures surrounding them. Mobile AtNBR1-positive lipid droplet remnants were also observed within the vacuole, particularly under treatments that simultaneously stimulate autophagy and limit vacuolar degradation. Besides, AtNBR1 degradation was modestly reduced in an atg2 mutant, which is consistent with a minor NBR1-associated macrolipophagy-like pathway. Moreover, AtNBR1 does not appear to mediate a major route of lipid droplet degradation, as loss of AtNBR1 did not significantly affect bulk lipid turnover or the degradation of ubiquitinated and non-ubiquitinated oleosins, the major seed lipid droplet proteins, arguing against oleosins being primary AtNBR1 cargoes. Instead, our data support a broader role for AtNBR1 in seed proteostasis. AtNBR1 interactome comprises multiple protein quality control components, including the post-proteasomal exopeptidase TPPII. AtNBR1 also colocalized with CDC48A and PUX10, components of the lipid droplet-associated degradation pathway, and PUX10 contributed to AtNBR1 turnover. Importantly, loss of AtNBR1 compromised seed longevity in an accelerated aging assay. Together, our findings suggest a role for AtNBR1 in protein quality control at lipid droplets and support its positive contribution to seed longevity.

papers.title: Oxidative stress and lipidocentric mechanism of hyperglycemic glycolaldehyde damage to skeletal muscle cells
papers.abstract: Currently, diabetes-induced skeletal muscle complications affect over half of diabetic patients yet the pathway by which this hyperglycemic damage occurs has yet to be fully elucidated. As such, the goal of this study is to investigate the hypothesis: Glucose-derived glycolaldehydes, glyoxal and methylglyoxal, formed in hyperglycemia cause damage to the skeletal muscle myoblasts through oxidative stress and formation of pro-inflammatory eicosanoids upon activation of phospholipase A2 (PLA2) and cyclooxygenase (COX). To test this hypothesis skeletal muscle myoblasts, C2C12s, were exposed to various concentrations of glyoxal and methylglyoxal then tested for metabolic activity, reactive oxygen species production, redox status, ATP production, membrane integrity, cellular proliferation, enzyme activity, and loss of mitochondrial lipids. Doses of the agonist at 1 mM and 2 mM showed significant changes in all tested areas and were significantly attenuated by NAC, Ibuprofen, AACOCF3 and metformin. For the first time, these results suggest a plausible pathway by which diabetes-induced skeletal muscle deterioration occurs and identifies possible therapeutic endpoints.

papers.title: Development of a Novel Multitarget Directed Ligand (MTDL), LCI132 for the Polypharmaceutical Treatment of High-Risk MYCN Amplified Neuroblastoma
papers.abstract: MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma (MNA-NB) is associated with poor prognosis due to the development of resistance to current aggressive therapy and to the subsequent limited response to single agent targeted therapeutics in the relapse setting. Herein, we describe the in silico design and development of the first-in-class nanomolar potent, selective, multitarget directed ligand (MTDL) against PI3K, BRD4, CDK4/6/9 and Aurora kinases A/B, LCI132, for the polypharmaceutical treatment of MNA-NB. LCI132 demonstrates a favorable safety and pharmacokinetics profile, suppresses viability, induces apoptosis in MNA-NB and inhibits in vivo tumor growth with no toxicity. Mechanistically our data show that LCI132 orthogonally inhibits MYCN transcription and induces proteasome mediated MYCN degradation. We and others recently observed an augmented cytostatic effect of combining CDK4/6 inhibitors with retinoic acid in MNA-NB models and the associated disruption of core regulatory circuits. Importantly, this was not associated with the induction of apoptosis. The combined treatment of MNA-NB cells with retinoic acid and LCI132 synergistically inhibited cellular proliferation and induced apoptosis in MNA-NB cell lines and ex vivo patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. Combination of LCI132 and ATRA treatment effectively reduces levels of MYCN and alters the expression of CRC transcription factors. Collectively, our study provides mechanistic insights and a rationale for the combined use of ATRA and a MTDL, LCI132 as a novel polypharmaceutical therapeutic strategy for the treatment of MNA-NB NB.

papers.title: The PD-L1 metabolic interactome in glioma is bounded by IDH1 genotype
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has failed in glioblastoma, and part of the reason may lie in the tumour cell itself: if the checkpoint and the metabolism that sustains the cell hold each other up, then lowering one arm hands the tumour the other, and a single agent cannot win. We tested that possibility in GL261 glioma cells of IDH1-wildtype and IDH1-mutant genotype, silencing Chka or Cd274, blocking PD-L1 with an antibody, and reading the consequences by RT-qPCR, RNA sequencing, flow cytometry of surface PD-L1 and high-resolution 1H NMR of dual-phase cell extracts. The two genes proved reciprocal in both genotypes: silencing either transcript raised the other, and silencing choline kinase roughly doubled PD-L1 at the cell surface. Antibody blockade did something the silencing did not. In IDH1-wildtype cells it lowered soluble phosphocholine, the only one of twenty-two aqueous signals to survive correction for multiple testing, and raised total lipid per cell without changing lipid composition, whereas silencing PD-L1 raised phosphocholine instead; in IDH1-mutant cells neither change occurred. The transcriptome drew the same boundary, engaging a sterol programme and lowering glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation in wild-type cells only. The interferon response did not respect that boundary and rose under every perturbation in both genotypes. Removing PD-L1 from inside the cell and blocking it from outside are therefore not the same intervention, and the metabolic half of the response stops at the IDH1 genotype.

papers.title: Single-agent PD-L1 blockade and tumour volume in orthotopic GL261 glioma, with an exploratory lipid analysis of the treated tumours
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has not yet changed outcomes in glioblastoma (GBM), and in immunocompetent mouse glioma the effect of a single blocking antibody is usually reported as survival rather than as tumour volume with its own confidence interval. We treated mice bearing orthotopic GL261 gliomas with anti-PD-L1 as a single agent in an IDH1-wild-type and in an IDH1-mutant line, and followed tumour volume by MRI. At day 14, tumours of treated animals were 0.33 times the volume of control tumours in the IDH1-wild-type line (95 % CI 0.21 to 0.53; p < 0.001; 16 anti-PD-L1 and 20 control animals) and 0.42 times in the IDH1-mutant line (0.22 to 0.78; p = 0.006; 10 and 10 animals), from a linear mixed model of log tumour volume over days 8 to 16. Diffusion imaging of the same tumours gave a higher apparent diffusion coefficient in the treated IDH1-wild-type tumours, by 23 % over the whole tumour (p = 0.027), and lower fractional anisotropy in the treated IDH1-mutant tumours, by 25 % over the whole tumour (p = 0.023), and in the periphery of the IDH1-wild-type ones, by 24 % (p = 0.005). We also imaged the lipid composition of treated and control IDH1-wild-type tumours ex vivo by mass spectrometry imaging: relative to the healthy brain of the same section, sphingomyelin was higher in the treated tumours and phosphatidylcholine species shifted towards shorter chains (p = 0.016 for both). In orthotopic GL261 glioma, anti-PD-L1 as a single agent reduces tumour volume in the IDH1-wild-type and in the IDH1-mutant line.

papers.title: FN1 is produced by cancer-associated fibroblasts and carries no immune-exclusion signal beyond the collagen program: a two-cohort single-cell re-examination in non-small cell lung cancer
papers.abstract: Fibronectin 1 (FN1) has been proposed as a macrophage-derived driver of T-cell exclusion and AP-1-mediated resistance to checkpoint blockade in lung cancer. The human evidence was never tested against the two confounders most likely to generate them: collagen/extracellular-matrix (ECM) abundance and dissociation-induced immediate-early gene (IEG) expression. We reanalyzed two public non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cohorts, GSE148071 (42 treatment-naive tumors) and GSE207422 (15 specimens; 92,330 cells), with 24 pre-treatment bulk transcriptomes. Malignant epithelium was called by compartment-level inferCNV; FN1 source was attributed within macrophage and fibroblast compartments and by ligand-receptor scoring; exclusion associations were tested by partial Spearman correlation with permutation testing, controlling for a 22-gene collagen/ECM signature; AP-1 regulon activity was quantified before and after masking the 27-gene IEG panel, benchmarked against a dissociation-stress score. FN1 was produced predominantly by cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs): the FN1-positive fraction was higher in CAFs than macrophages in both cohorts (paired Wilcoxon P = 1.6 x 10?? and P = 0.002), and CAF-to-epithelium communication exceeded macrophage-to-epithelium by about six-fold (median 0.32 vs 0.05, P = 1.5 x 10??). An independent lung-adenocarcinoma cohort (GSE131907) replicated this cell of origin (FN1-positive fraction 0.88 in CAFs versus 0.44 in TAMs; 11 paired samples, P = 0.001). The bulk FN1-cytotoxic association ({rho} = -0.53, P = 0.008) disappeared after collagen adjustment across three independent FN1 scoring schemes (partial {rho} = +0.21 to -0.16, all P > 0.33) and was not reproduced at single-cell level. Sample-level AP-1 activity tracked dissociation stress ({rho} = 0.88, P = 2.3 x 10??); IEG masking shrank histology-associated effect sizes by 40-64%, yet masked activity remained stress-coupled ({rho} = 0.82). FN1 is therefore a CAF product whose apparent link to immune exclusion is absorbed by the collagen program, and AP-1 readouts from dissociated tissue are stress-dominated; stress scores should accompany AP-1-based resistance claims.

papers.title: Multimodal Virtual Screening Identifies Candidate Inhibitors of Polyploid Giant Cancer Cells Across Breast Cancer Subtypes
papers.abstract: Polyploid giant cancer cells (PGCCs) are associated with treatment resistance and tumor recurrence yet identifying compounds that selectively suppress these cells remains challenging. Here, we developed a multimodal machine-learning framework to prioritize PGCC-suppressing compounds by integrating chemical fingerprints, drug-induced cellular morphology, transcriptomic perturbation profiles, and biologically informed molecular annotations. Using screening data from four breast cancer cell lines, we systematically evaluated feature selection, drug representations, and ensemble learning strategies. PGCC-guided feature selection reduced morphology dimensionality by 93.7% while identifying cell-cycle-enriched gene sets, linking predictive features to biologically relevant processes. An ensemble integrating complementary predictors achieved a mean Pearson correlation of 0.403 and an enrichment factor of 5.46 among the top 5% of ranked compounds. In held-out screening data, the ensemble recovered 27.9% of experimentally identified hits, representing approximately 5.6-fold and 2.5-fold improvements over random selection and the best individual predictor, respectively. We subsequently prioritized 21,367 compounds from an external library for experimental evaluation. Experimental testing identified six candidates that preferentially suppressed PGCCs in at least three paclitaxel-treated cell lines. Notably, AZD-8055 and voxtalisib reduced PGCC abundance by at least 70% across all four cell lines. These results establish a multimodal computational-experimental strategy for phenotype-directed drug discovery and provide new candidates for targeting treatment-induced PGCCs.
